<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>I</c>ubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>L</c>et us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro primo Machabæórum
<r>1 Mac 2:69-70; 3:1-2</r>
<n>69</n> Et benedíxit eos (Mathathías) et appósitus est ad patres suos.
<n>70</n> Et defúnctus est anno centésimo et quadragésimo sexto: et sepúltus est a fíliis suis in sepúlcris patrum suórum in Modin, et planxérunt eum omnis Israël planctu magno.
<n>1</n> Et surréxit Judas, qui vocabátur Machabǽus, fílius ejus, pro eo:
<n>2</n> Et adjuvábant eum omnes fratres ejus, et univérsi qui se conjúnxerant patri ejus, et prœliabántur prœ́lium Israël cum lætítia.

<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Adapériat Dóminus cor vestrum in lege sua et in præcéptis suis et fáciat pacem in diébus vestris:
* Concédat vobis salútem, et rédimat vos a malis.

<r>℟.</r> Concédat vobis salútem, et rédimat vos a malis.

b.241940c3c2:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uarto Idus Octóbris Luna duodécima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ sanctórum Mártyrum Evágrii, Prisciáni, et Sociórum.
<h>I</h>n Africa sanctórum Confessórum et Mártyrum quátuor míllium nongentórum sexagínta sex, in persecutióne Wandálica, sub Hunneríco, Rege Ariáno. Hi, cum essent partim Epíscopi Ecclesiárum Dei, partim Presbýteri et Diáconi, associátis sibi turbis fidélium populórum, pro defensióne cathólicæ veritátis in horríbilis erémi exsílium trusi sunt; ex quibus plúrimi, dum crudéliter a Mauris duceréntur, hastílium cuspídibus impúlsi ad curréndum et lapídibus tunsi, álii, ligátis pédibus, velut cadávera per dura et áspera loca tracti et síngulis membris discérpti, ad extrémum, várie excruciáti, martýrium celebrárunt. Erant inter eos præcípui Sacerdótes Dómini, Felix et Cypriánus Epíscopi.
<h>R</h>avénnæ, via Laurentína, natális sancti Edístii Mártyris.
<h>I</h>n Lýcia sanctæ Domnínæ Mártyris, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
<h>C</h>elénæ, in Pannónia, sancti Maximiliáni, Epíscopi Laureacénsis.
<h>E</h>boráci, in Anglia, sancti Walfrídi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>M</h>edioláni sancti Monæ Epíscopi, qui, cum de Epíscopo eligéndo agerétur, cælésti lúmine circumfúsus, eo signo mirabíliter in Pontíficem illíus Ecclésiæ est assúmptus.
<h>V</h>erónæ sancti Salvíni Epíscopi.
<h>I</h>n Sýria sancti Eustáchii, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
<h>A</h>sculi, in Picéno, sancti Seraphíni Confessóris, ex Ordine Minórum Capuccinórum, vitæ sanctimónia et humilitáte conspícui; quem Clemens Décimus tértius, Póntifex Máximus, Sanctórum fastis adscrípsit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.402a53f1db:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>O</c>ctober 12th 2027, the 12th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Confessor Wilfred, Bishop of York.
<h>U</h>pon the same 12th day of October, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyrs Evagrius, Priscian, and their Companions.
<h>I</h>n Africa are commemorated four thousand nine hundred and sixty-six holy martyrs and Confessors in the Vandal persecution under the Arian King Hunneric. Some of these were Bishops of the Churches of God, and some of them Priests and Deacons, but with them were joined multitudes of the other faithful. For defending the Catholic truth they were driven into exile in the terrible desert many of them were cruelly taken by the Moors, goaded to run at the point of the spear, and beaten with stones others had their feet tied together, and were dragged like corpses through hard and sharp places, until all their limbs were mangled and then were tortured to death in diverse ways. Pre-eminent among them were the Bishops Felix and Cyprian.
<h>A</h>t Ravenna, on the Laurentine Way, (in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian,) the holy martyr Edistius.
<h>I</h>n Lycia, under the same Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyr Domnina.
<h>A</h>t Celeia, in Pannonia, (in the fourth century,) holy Maximilian, Bishop (of Lorch.)
<h>A</h>t Milan, (in the third century,) the holy Bishop Monas. During the discussion as to the choosing of a Bishop there, a light from heaven shone upon him, and through that wondrous sign he was made Bishop of that church.
<h>A</h>t Verona, holy Salvin, Bishop.
<h>I</h>n Syria, the holy Priest and Confessor Eustace.
<h>A</h>t Ascoli, in the March of Ancona, (in the year 1604,) the holy Confessor Seraphim, of the Order of Friars Minor Capuchins, who was marked by holiness of life and by lowliness, and whose name the Supreme Pontiff Clement XIII enrolled with those of the Saints.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
